title: User account
purpose: Create or maintain a staff or client account while preserving attributed laboratory history.
summary: Create or change one staff or client account: identity, client link, role groups, permissions and active state.

tasks.title: Create an account
steps: Enter [[Username]] and [[Email address]], then set a password or turn off password-based authentication.
For a client portal user, choose the [[Client]] (opening Add portal account on a client organization's page chooses it for you). For staff, leave it blank and choose [[Groups]].
Select [[Save]]. The form reopens with the remaining options.

tasks.title: Give or remove a role
steps: Move groups between Available groups and Chosen groups under [[Groups]], then select [[Save]].

tasks.title: Grant a capability
steps: Under [[User permissions]], choose the accounts permission Can view patient information, or add a group that grants it. Then save.
For access needed only for a while, give it under [[User permissions]] and set its last day under Capability end dates. After that day it gives nothing.

tasks.title: Stop someone from signing in
steps: Under Account status and technical access, select [[Deactivate]], check what the account holds, give a reason and confirm.
Clearing [[Active]] and saving also deactivates it; what it held is recorded, without a reason. Accounts are never deleted.

tasks.title: Sign someone out everywhere
steps: Under Sessions, select [[End sessions]], give a reason and confirm. The person can sign in again unless you also deactivate the account.

good_to_know: Staff status and Superuser status grant no laboratory role and no capability.
Clear the client link before giving an account staff flags, groups or permissions.
You cannot deactivate the last active staff superuser or remove their Staff or Superuser status. The Scheduled jobs account cannot be changed.
If someone else saved the account after you opened it, your save is refused and nothing changes. Open the account again and redo your change.
Saving asks you to confirm it is you (your password, a code, or both, as the page asks), unless you confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. Changes are audited without passwords.

sections.title: Access and page variants
paragraphs: The administration site requires an active account with Staff status. User and group pages additionally require Superuser status; a laboratory admin role alone or individual model permissions do not open them. These technical flags do not themselves confer operational roles or capabilities.

Add user includes Username, Email address, Password-based authentication, Password, Password confirmation, Client, Groups, Staff status and Superuser status. New users default to Active even though Active is not on this add form. After creation the change form exposes the remaining account options. Change user groups fields into Personal info, Client access, Laboratory roles, Account status and technical access, Capability end dates, Important dates (read only) and Sessions (read only); Compromised password (read only) follows Password, and Deactivation (read only) opens Account status and technical access.
On both forms, while saving asks you to confirm it is you, a Confirm it is you section follows the fields, before the buttons (see Confirm it is you).

items.label: Username
items.description: Required unique identifier, at most 150 characters; Unicode letters and digits plus @/./+/-/_ are accepted. Saving creation rejects case-insensitive duplicates; ordinary edit uses the model’s exact username uniqueness constraint.

items.label: Email address
items.description: Required syntactically valid unique account email in both add and change forms. This field is not an EmailAddress verification record or a client contact. Creation does not send an invitation or verification email.

items.label: Password-based authentication
items.description: Creation only: Enabled by default or Disabled. Enabled requires both password fields; Disabled sets an unusable password and ignores them. No alternative login provider is configured by this choice.

items.label: Password / Password confirmation
items.description: Creation: required matching password when Enabled. A new account's first password needs at least 15 characters whatever the second sign-in factor rule, and common and expected passwords and ones too similar to the username or email address are refused. No required kinds of character.

items.label: Password
items.description: Change only: read-only password-hash status, never the original secret. Reset password or Set password opens the separate administrator password form; changing this display is not password entry. The Scheduled jobs account shows its status only: nobody signs in as it, and no password can be set.

items.label: Compromised password
items.description: Change only; read only. Whether the account's password is marked as compromised now: when and by whom, while the person must choose a new one, or Not marked with the Mark as compromised link, which opens a page to mark it with a reason. Shows why instead on your own account (change your own password instead), for a shared demonstration account or for an account without a password; the Scheduled jobs account shows a dash. Any new password lifts the mark.

items.label: First name / Last name
items.description: Change only; optional, each at most 150 characters, used for operator display and searching.

items.label: Client
items.description: Optional client selection. Blank means internal laboratory account; a selected client limits portal records to that client. Clear the link before granting staff flags, groups or permissions. Related-object maintenance shortcuts appear only when their registered model and permission allow them. Changing the client of an account that has portal access resets that access, recorded in its history: no linked contact, no sites, not the whole organization. The account then sees only the tickets it raised until staff set its access again on the organization's page. An account stays a laboratory account or a client portal account for life: setting a client on a laboratory account, or clearing it on a portal account, is refused; create a new account instead.

items.label: Groups
items.description: Optional assigned groups in Available groups and Chosen groups, with filter boxes, choose/remove controls and Choose all/Remove all. Built-in group names determine roles. Custom groups can carry explicit permissions without becoming operational roles. Removing a role or a capability waits for a change the person is saving at that moment, which is kept; a change they start afterwards no longer has that role or capability. A role or a group's Can view patient information grant can bring the account under the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule (Security settings), from its next sign-in.

items.label: Deactivation
items.description: Change only; read only, first under Account status and technical access. The account's latest deactivation record: Deactivated on a date and time (in the display time zone) by the username of whoever saved it, as that account is named now, or by an account that was not recorded when the save named nobody, with how many open tickets were returned to their team queues when there were any; Reason: the reason given on Deactivate (on your own account's page, A reason was recorded. It is not shown on your own account's page.), or No reason was recorded when the account was deactivated by clearing Active or by another path; and What it held when it was deactivated: its kind and organization, then its portal access, or its admin console access, roles, capabilities with how each was held, and teams, as they stood then. An account made active again since shows the same record, starting Made active again since it was deactivated on. An inactive account with no record says What it held then was not recorded: it was deactivated before deactivations were recorded, or by a path that records none. An active account shows the Deactivate link, which opens a page to see what it holds and deactivate it with a reason; on your own account the line says This is your own account. Another superuser can deactivate it. instead. The Scheduled jobs account shows a dash. A record is never changed or deleted.

items.label: Active
items.description: Change only; controls whether the account may authenticate and have operational access. Deactivate the account (the Deactivate link under Deactivation) or clear this instead of deleting a historical contributor. Clearing it records what the account held just before this save, including roles and capabilities removed in the same save, without a reason, shown under Deactivation. Clearing it also returns the person's tickets that are not closed to their teams' queues, unassigned, and the confirmation says how many; a ticket assigned to them while you save is either returned with the others or refused. A change the person is saving at that moment, such as a note, finishes first and your save waits for it; one they start after it is refused. A client's reply on one of their tickets that is being saved at that moment is kept, and the ticket is still returned to the queue. Ticking it again makes a deactivated account active with every role, capability, team membership and portal access it kept, which then give access again, apart from a capability or portal access whose last day has passed; its sessions stay ended.

items.label: Staff status
items.description: Allows the maintenance-site entry check; does not grant laboratory roles, superuser status or model permissions. Where the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule covers accounts that can open the admin console, an account with Staff status must also set up an authenticator app at its next sign-in.

items.label: Superuser status
items.description: Enables Django permission bypass for administration; does not grant laboratory roles or any capability.

items.label: User permissions
items.description: Change only. Available user permissions/Chosen user permissions assign explicit capabilities, such as the accounts permission Can view patient information. Groups can grant the same capability. Neither a role, the admin role nor Superuser status implies one, and model permissions do not replace laboratory role or ownership checks. Removing a capability waits for a change the person is saving at that moment. Removing a capability given directly also removes its last day, and a capability given anew starts with none.

items.label: Last day of “Can view patient information” / Last day of “Can review access and audit records”
items.description: Change only, under Capability end dates; optional, one date for each capability. It applies only to the capability given to the account directly (ticked under User permissions); a capability given through a role or group has no end date. A day for a capability not given directly is refused: Give this capability to the account directly (under User permissions), or clear its last day. A newly chosen day must be today or later: Choose today or a later day. To end it now, remove it instead. It must also be within the next 100 years: Choose a day within the next 100 years, or leave it empty for no end. A day left as the page showed it, even one already past, is never refused and keeps the end as saved, even if the laboratory's time zone changed after the page opened. Leave empty for no end.

items.label: When a last day ends
items.description: The grant gives nothing from the start of the next day in the laboratory's time zone (the deployment's time zone as set when the day is saved; the moment is stored, so a later time-zone change does not move it). Every check compares the end with the database's clock: the sidebar items, every page and action that needs the capability (patient information shown or revealed, Audit review and Access review), the second sign-in factor rule for holders of Can view patient information, the holder counts on Security settings, the access report's capability filter and the access review. The ended grant stays on the account, giving nothing, until you remove it or set a later day, which gives it again. Its field's help then starts with Ended. The Capabilities column of the Users list leaves out an ended grant.

items.label: Setting or moving a last day
items.description: Takes away access like a removal: a change the person is saving at that moment finishes first; one they start afterwards is checked against the new end. Nothing reminds anyone before an end, and nothing removes an ended grant automatically.

items.label: Last login
items.description: Change only; read only. The date and time the person last finished signing in, recorded by the application. It is not a complete login history.

items.label: Date joined
items.description: Change only; read only. The date and time the account was created.

items.label: Open sessions
items.description: Change only; read only, under Sessions. How many sessions of the account are open and inside the session limits when the page opens, never their browsers or addresses, with the End sessions link, which opens a page to end them all with a reason. Ending sessions does not ask you to confirm it is you. The Scheduled jobs account shows the count without the link.

sections.title: Integrity and history
paragraphs: Client isolation, last-active-superuser preservation and immutable historical actors are checked by this administration implementation. Existing built-in groups cannot be renamed in group editing. Capabilities such as viewing patient information are held only through an explicit permission. Account/role changes are audited with before/after snapshots; secret values are omitted. The change form carries the account as it was drawn. Saving waits for another change of the account being saved at that moment, then compares: if anything the page shows has changed since it was drawn, the save is refused and nothing is recorded, so a page opened earlier cannot put back an older email, name, role or status. The comparison is with the values the page was drawn with; roles count by which ones the account holds, so renaming a role on the role group page changes no account and does not refuse it. Roles and permissions are saved as the difference between those values and your choices, so a role given by other means after the comparison is kept. The audit's before values are the account as read under that wait, and its after values are what this save made. When the account has or had a capability last day, the change event also records the ends before and after.

sections.title: Confirm it is you
paragraphs: Every save on Add user and Change user, whatever it changes (names, email address, client, groups, flags or permissions), asks you, the person signed in, to confirm it is you, unless you already confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. The Confirm it is you section then appears before the buttons, and nothing is saved until what you type there is accepted. Signing in does not count: only confirming again does, and a new sign-in, even in the same browser, starts without one. Once you have confirmed, no page that asks (account administration, and the session limits and second sign-in factor rule on Security settings) asks again in this browser for 5 minutes. A page opened while you were confirmed and saved after the 5 minutes passed asks then.

Confirming on Confirm your password, or with a code before a change to your own two-factor settings, counts too, once every factor your account has was given there within the last 5 minutes: each counts for 5 minutes from when it was given, so the earlier one runs out first. A confirmation here counts for those pages as well. A new password, or a new or different authenticator app, on your account since you confirmed makes the next save ask again, for both. An account with neither a password nor an authenticator app cannot confirm, so it cannot save here until it sets a password.

When the confirmation is missing or not accepted, nothing is saved, and no audit event or administration history entry is written. What you typed in the other fields stays on the page, except the new account's passwords. A confirmation accepted while another field is refused is kept: the page shows that field's error without the section, and saving again within the 5 minutes does not ask.

A password or code not accepted is listed in your own Sign-in history as Re-authentication failed and counts toward the failed sign-in limit; an attempt that limit refuses is listed as Too many failed attempts. What you type in these fields is never stored, logged or put in an audit event, and the administration history does not list it among the changed fields.

items.label: Your password
items.description: Shown when your account has a password: your own current password, not the password of the account you are changing or creating. The help under it says what saving asks for and that you are not asked again in this browser for 5 minutes. Left empty: Enter your password to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect password. Accepted, but the code is not: Enter your password again with the code (the page does not keep it).

items.label: Authenticator or recovery code
items.description: Shown when your account has an authenticator app: a code from it, or one of your unused recovery codes, which is then used up. Left empty: Enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code, to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect code. The password is checked first; when it is not accepted, the code is not checked and can still be used.

items.label: Too many failed login attempts. Try again later.
items.description: The failed sign-in limit refused your password or code before checking it, after too many that were not accepted. Wait a few minutes, then try again.

items.label: Too many attempts to confirm it is you. Wait a minute, then try again.
items.description: Shown after 10 tries within a minute by your account (the Confirm your password pages count too). Nothing was checked, and the refusal is not listed in Sign-in history.

items.label: Your account has no password to confirm it is you, so this change cannot be saved. Set a password on Change password first.
items.description: Your account has neither a password nor an authenticator app, so it has nothing to confirm with. Set a password from Change password in the account menu, then save again.

items.label: Your sign-in factors changed, or your confirmation ran out, while this page was open. Confirm it is you again.
items.description: An authenticator app was added to or removed from your account, or your confirmation ran out, while your save was being checked. Nothing is saved. The section now asks for what your account has: fill it in and save again.

items.label: Save
items.description: Asks you to confirm it is you first, unless you did in this browser in the last 5 minutes (see Confirm it is you); so do Save and continue editing and Save and add another. On Add user, saves and normally opens the new change form so you can edit remaining options. On Change user, saves and returns to the user list. Popup creation returns the selection to its opener. On Change user, the save is refused with the message that someone else saved this account when any value the page shows (username, names, email, client, groups, permissions, a capability's last day, Active, Staff status or Superuser status) changed after you opened it, by another administrator, the person or the application; nothing is saved. Open the account again to see the current values. A change of the password or the sign-in time meanwhile does not refuse the save and is kept: a save writes only the fields this page edits.

items.label: Save and continue editing
items.description: Saves and opens the user change form.

items.label: Save and add another
items.description: Saves and starts a new user add form.

items.label: History
items.description: Change only: opens Django object administration history.

items.label: Delete
items.description: Never available for users; direct deletion is refused.

items.label: Home / app / Users / View site
items.description: Breadcrumbs return through administration; View site returns to the operational application. Validation errors retain non-secret form input for correction.
